hero.title: File:This Horror Must End.jpg
hero.artist: Anonymous author and anonymous British soldier photographers
hero.credit: 10 May 1952, Daily Worker (Morning Star), front page article
hero.description:
This Horror Must End was a news article published by the Daily Worker (later renamed Morning Star) exposing never before published photographs of British forces and their Iban headhunter allies engaging in atrocities during the Malayan Emergency (1948-1960). The collection of scalps and severed heads was a common practice performed by British troops and their allies during the war.
These photographs were published by British communist activists in the hopes that they would turn public opinion against the British occupation of Malaya.

This article is the third article published by the Daily Worker in 1952 which contained never before published images of headhunting by British forces in Malaya.
categories: War crimes committed by the United Kingdom

gallery.title: File:Headhunters Malayan Emergency.jpg
gallery.description:
A photograph of British allied headhunters in a Royal Marine base posing with the severed head of a suspected pro-independence guerrilla, likely belonging to the Malayan National Liberation Army (MNLA).
This image was first published on 30 April 1952 by the Daily Worker, a British communist newspaper which was later renamed the Morning Star. This image was published in response to British government and military claims that a previous decapitation photograph published by the Daily Worker on the 28 April 1952 was fake.
categories: War crimes committed by the United Kingdom
